summary: Light-ion flow as a constraint on chiral nuclear forces and ALICE event-shape-engineered flow correlations lead the heavy-ion selection. Small-system collectivity remains statistically unresolved at the lowest multiplicities, while quarkyonic-matter evidence is coherent but indirect. Physics AI/ML is led by better evaluation of conditional generative surrogates and rigorous coverage limits for time-dependent PDE emulators.
professional_summary: Chiral-force sensitivity in light ions, nonlinear flow response in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe, low-multiplicity identified-particle flow, quarkyonic saturation, Lévy femtoscopy extraction, conditional-surrogate scoring, and conformal uncertainty for PDE rollouts define the selected literature.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2611.08122 is the strongest theory/phenomenology bridge because it maps light-ion geometry to chiral-EFT couplings with ab initio emulators; arXiv:2611.08473 is the strongest measurement; arXiv:2611.07826 provides the most immediately actionable HEP ML evaluation result.

papers.title: Linking chiral nuclear forces to light-ion collisions: a global sensitivity analysis
papers.short_authors: Thomas Duguet, Andreas Ekström, Giuliano Giacalone, Gaute Hagen, Takayuki Miyagi, Alexander Tichai
papers.abstract: Ultrarelativistic 16O+16O and 20Ne+20Ne collisions are connected quantitatively to the low-energy constants of chiral inter-nucleon interactions. Subspace-projected coupled-cluster emulators show that the quadrupole mean-square eccentricity responds approximately linearly and additively to all 16 NNLO low-energy constants, with 20Ne particularly sensitive to the two-nucleon spin-orbit contact.
papers.summary: This is the strongest conceptual bridge in today's batch: flow observables become complementary constraints on nuclear forces rather than only probes of bulk geometry.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong and genuinely novel, with ab initio many-body calculations, emulation, and a global sensitivity analysis. The current result is a sensitivity map, not yet an extraction from data: many-body and EFT-truncation uncertainties, hydrodynamic response uncertainty, and the dominant one-body contribution still need to enter a full Bayesian inference.

papers.title: Hypersurface covariance in relativistic local equilibrium
papers.short_authors: You-yu Li, Shuai Y. F. Liu
papers.abstract: Using spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions, the authors argue that hypersurface dependence in the local-equilibrium part of the Zubarev density operator is canceled by a previously omitted nondissipative contribution from the nominally dissipative part. The resulting framework is hypersurface covariant while retaining a physical medium-frame dependence.
papers.summary: The work targets a real formal inconsistency behind competing treatments of Lambda-hyperon polarization and supplies a compact covariant resolution.
papers.critical_assessment: Conceptually important and technically focused, but the evidence is mainly formal. Its impact will depend on independent checks of the bookkeeping and on whether implementation changes quantitative polarization predictions; no new data comparison is provided.

papers.title: Has Quarkyonic Matter Been Seen in Lattice Simulations?
papers.short_authors: Kohei Fujikura, Kenji Fukushima, Yoshimasa Hidaka, Etsuko Itou, Larry McLerran
papers.abstract: A 63-page synthesis compares distribution-function expectations for quarkyonic matter with two-color lattice QCD at finite baryon density, QCD at finite isospin density, and astrophysically inferred equations of state. The authors find a coherent pattern compatible with quarkyonic saturation and propose direct momentum-distribution measurements as the decisive next test.
papers.summary: The paper is a serious, useful consolidation of lattice-accessible evidence for an intermediate confined but quark-dominated regime.
papers.critical_assessment: Worth reading, but the title is stronger than the evidence. The authors themselves state that thermodynamics alone does not establish quark-occupation saturation; only the 1+1-dimensional two-color case offers a relatively direct distribution-level test, while the 3+1-dimensional and astrophysical evidence remains interpretive.

papers.title: Correlations and fluctuations of flow with event shape engineering in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC
papers.abstract: ALICE measures correlations among v2, v3, and v4 in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions and separates linear and nonlinear v4 components with event-shape engineering and multiparticle correlators. The nonlinear component tracks initial ellipticity strongly, while the linear component is nearly independent of it; chi4,22 is mostly stable against q2 selection.
papers.summary: This is the day's strongest direct heavy-ion measurement, supplying differential constraints on initial geometry, flow fluctuations, and nonlinear hydrodynamic response across two system sizes.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong experimental work with complementary extraction methods, rapidity gaps, fine centrality selection, and detailed systematic variations. Interpretation still inherits assumptions used in the linear/nonlinear decomposition and residual nonflow sensitivity, especially in the smaller Xe-Xe sample, but the observable-level result is robust.

papers.title: Exploring the limit of partonic collectivity in small collision systems at the LHC
papers.abstract: ALICE extends identified-particle v2 measurements in p-Pb and pp collisions to lower multiplicity. Clear mass ordering and baryon-meson splitting persist for Nch >= 25, while the lowest bin yields only about 2 sigma evidence in p-Pb and less than 1 sigma in pp.
papers.summary: The measurement narrows the empirical boundary where heavy-ion-like identified-particle flow patterns become statistically unresolved.
papers.critical_assessment: The analysis is valuable and appropriately cautious. It does not locate a collectivity threshold: low-multiplicity p-Pb is marginal and pp is inconclusive, and baryon-meson splitting is evidence consistent with coalescence rather than a unique proof of a partonic phase. Run 3 precision will be decisive.

papers.title: Comparison of Methods for Extracting Three-Dimensional Lévy Source Parameters in 200 GeV Au+Au Collisions with EPOS3
papers.short_authors: Máté Szilágyi, Máté Csanád, Dániel Kincses
papers.abstract: Four extraction routes for 3D Lévy source parameters are compared on EPOS3 Au+Au events. Direct numerical integration and FFT agree to RMSE below 10^-14, with FFT reducing hours to seconds, while correlation-function fits yield systematic 7-9% shifts in the Lévy index relative to direct source fits.
papers.summary: The main value is methodological: it exposes analysis-definition effects that can masquerade as physical source-shape differences and provides a much faster numerically equivalent implementation.
papers.critical_assessment: Useful and transparent, but limited to generator-level EPOS3 and a workshop contribution. The discrepancy is plausibly traced to non-Lévy features and ensemble mixing, yet experimental Coulomb corrections, detector effects, and model dependence are not resolved.

papers.title: Estimating Spectrum-Free Information Bounds for Generative Surrogates Beyond Conditional Collapse
papers.abstract: On a CMS simulation benchmark, a condition-blind sampler can beat trained conditional generators on common one-dimensional marginal divergences. The paper replaces these with CRPS-based skill scores and a k-nearest-neighbor extrapolation estimating how much predictive information the conditioner contains.
papers.summary: This directly improves how fast-simulation and reconstruction surrogates should be evaluated in HEP: passing marginal plots is shown to be compatible with ignoring the conditioning event.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong because it demonstrates a concrete evaluation failure, proposes a proper-score alternative, and states its limits. The ceiling is estimated rather than proven, all reported scores are one-dimensional, correlations between outputs remain untested, and the numerical conclusions are benchmark-specific.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
papers.short_authors: Joshua Stiller, Annika Schneider, Eyke Hüllermeier
papers.abstract: The paper proves that exact conformal coverage can fail sharply for time-dependent PDE surrogate models: distributions at arbitrarily close times may be mutually singular, and discretized total-variation distance can saturate exponentially with grid resolution. Under restricted settings, weighted conformal prediction restores finite-sample coverage over growing horizons.
papers.summary: The transfer value is clear for learned hydrodynamic and transport emulators used in heavy-ion inference, where temporal rollout and finer grids can silently invalidate nominal uncertainty coverage.
papers.critical_assessment: A strong theoretical warning with constructive results and NeurIPS acceptance. Transfer to HEP or nuclear physics is methodological rather than demonstrated; the useful guarantees require assumptions and discretization restrictions that must be checked for each simulator and deployment distribution.
